correctness.rationale: PASS: Independently followed the all-word converse, not merely existence of a two-permutation representation. Rotate at a symbol x of a part A to xUxV. Every outside symbol occurs once in U and V, two outside parts maintain interpart order to alternate, whereas symbols within a part reverse order; an interleaving of the same part with an outside part would contradict these requirements, forcing part-contiguous blocks. Extra A symbols occur twice in U or V and must bracket every outside symbol and nest within A, which yields the displayed cyclic normal form. The converse follows pairwise. The word is rotationally primitive unless every pair alternates (excluded noncomplete graph); each orbit has exactly 2r part-boundary cuts yielding normalized forms. Counting r! product n_i! block choices gives both formulas. Independently enumerated all 113400 distinct 5-label double-occurrence linear words, all 2520 4-label words, and checked n_i profiles (2,1,1), (1,2,1), (2,1,1,1), (2,2,1), (3,1,1) against exact factorial values 16,16,60,40,60. Finite verification is not an all-r proof.

value.rationale: PASS: Complete multipartite graphs are a canonical nontrivial family of circle/word-representable graphs. Classifying all their labeled two-uniform representation words and exact rotational orbits is a natural finite-alphabet combinatorial invariant, and the universal forced-block theorem is strictly stronger than finding one witness.

final_claim: For labeled complete multipartite graphs with r>=3 nonempty parts and at least one nonsingleton part, every twice-occurring word representing the interlacement graph is a cyclic rotation of B1...Br B1^rev...Br^rev for a permutation of part order and of labels in each block. The number of labeled linear such words is N(r-1)! product n_i!, and rotation classes number ((r-1)!/2) product n_i!.
limitations: Requires at least three nonempty parts and a nonsingleton; no count modulo reflection or vertex relabeling.
